1	# ADR-020: Declarative package convergence — (name, origin) replicates; repository configuration is derived
2	
3	Status: Draft
4	
5	Date: 2026-07-23
6	
7	## TL;DR
8	
9	The source captures a manifest; the target diffs its own state against it and converges via `apt`, `snap` and `flatpak` themselves. Package databases are never rsynced. A package replicates as **(name, origin)**, not name alone. Seven independent jobs each run plan → review → apply inside their own `execute()`. Repositories, keys, pins, flatpak remotes and blocks (apt holds, snap refresh holds, flatpak masks) are derived from the packages approved from them and never reviewed directly.
10	
11	## Context
12	
13	Package sync must replicate presence, version and provenance of packages across apt, snap and flatpak, plus the repository/keyring/pin/remote configuration those installs depend on. Application data belongs to `folder_sync`.
14	
15	Provenance is the hard part: `firefox` exists in Ubuntu's archive and in Mozilla's own repository; `org.mozilla.firefox` on Flathub and Flathub-beta. Matching by name alone replicates the name and inverts the provenance, silently, at exit 0.
16	
17	## Decision
18	
19	### D-01 — Convergence model
20	
21	Source captures a manifest; target diffs and converges via the ecosystem's own tools. `/var/lib/dpkg`, `/var/lib/snapd` and the flatpak OSTree store are never rsynced.
22	
23	### D-02 — Item model
24	
25	An item is something the user can decide about. Item classes: apt package, apt config file, snap, snap channel, flatpak ref, unreproducible install; for removal only, apt source and pin files. Flatpak remotes and blocks (holds, masks) are derived, not items.
26	
27	### D-03/D-04/D-05 — Version and manifest policy
28	
29	Apt manifest carries `apt-mark showmanual`. Versions float; a mismatch is `REPORT_ONLY`. Held apt packages take the source's exact version — a hold blocks install, upgrade and removal alike.
30	
31	### D-06 — Snap converges revision and channel
32	
33	Snap embeds the version in its per-user data path (`~/snap/<app>/<rev>`), so both machines must be on the same revision for `folder_sync` to mirror snap data cleanly. Snapd's automatic refresh is paused across the sync window on both hosts with a timeout, and each host's prior setting is restored on cleanup.
34	
35	### D-07 — Decision shape
36	
37	Three-way by default: apply / skip once / skip always. Two-way (act / skip once, no record) for apt source removal, apt pin removal and repository-conflict overwrite prompts. `REPORT_ONLY` takes no answer.
38	
39	### D-08 — Machine-local decision file
40	
41	One file per manager at `~/.config/pc-switcher/<manager>.decisions.yaml`, never synced. An entry on machine M makes the item inert on M in both roles. An entry is dropped once M no longer has the item; a dead entry would refuse the item's return.
42	
43	### D-11 through D-14 — `/etc/apt` is derived, not mirrored
44	
45	Four buckets: derived from approved packages (repository files, keyrings, conflict-free overwrites); always synced (`preferences.d` pins, distribution source files); reviewed two-way (repository and pin removals, repository-conflict overwrite); reviewed three-way (`apt.conf.d`). Only files apt itself reads. Keys travel byte-for-byte from the source, never re-fetched. Derived writes precede the installs that need them.
46	
47	### D-15 — Seven separate jobs
48	
49	`apt_sync`, `snap_sync`, `flatpak_sync`, `manual_deb_sync`, `manual_snap_sync`, `manual_flatpak_sync`, `manual_installs_sync` are seven separate `SyncJob`s over one shared core. Each ships disabled. No review spans two managers. All seven run before `folder_sync`.
50	
51	### D-22 — Unreproducible items
52	
53	Each item has two mandatory bodies: `install_body` (replayed on the target) and `version_body` (prints the installed version on whichever machine runs it). Version comparison drives convergence; there is no folder diff and no payload hash. `version_body` runs on both machines during `plan()`, ungated by `--confirm-each-command`. Replay loops until versions match or the user skips. No purge-and-retry answer; no uninstall snippets.
54	
55	### D-24 — Batched review, rounds when correctness needs them
56	
57	Each job runs plan → review → apply in its own `execute()`. One screen per manager per action where the logic permits. `apt_sync` may ask in up to three rounds — the second round asks questions scoped to APPROVED work; the third asks collateral for an install whose repository this run itself writes.
58	
59	### D-30 / D-40 — Collateral protects the target's `apt-mark showmanual`
60	
61	apt collateral affecting the target's own manually-installed set becomes its own reviewable item (act / skip now / stop the sync). Only APPROVED removals waive the protection.
62	
63	### D-34 / D-35 — (name, origin) enforced at the target's real state
64	
65	The unit of replication for apt is (name, origin). After the `/etc/apt` group's single `apt-get update` and before the first install, one batched `apt-cache policy` re-reads target candidate origins; an install whose candidates do not intersect the source's fails as its own item. Distribution origins are per-machine exempt.
66	
67	### D-36 — Pins always-sync
68	
69	`preferences.d` pin adds and updates sync silently. A pin naming an absent origin is inert.
70	
71	### D-38 — Distribution source files and ESM
72	
73	`ubuntu.sources`, `/etc/apt/sources.list`, `ubuntu-esm-apps.sources`, `ubuntu-esm-infra.sources` are written when missing, overwritten when different, never removed. When the two ESM files would be written and the target reports unattached, `apt_sync` asks (attach and re-probe / skip `apt_sync`); non-interactive runs take the skip. pc-switcher cannot attach on the user's behalf.
74	
75	### D-41 — Flatpak remotes derived from refs
76	
77	A flatpak remote travels because an approved ref names it in that ref's scope. Ref identity is `<application>/<arch>/<branch>`; origin stays out of identity, so a ref on both machines from different remotes is `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` and never converged. Origin is compared by URL, never remote name.
78	
79	### D-42 — Snap: nothing to derive
80	
81	One store per device, name→publisher pinned by canonical-signed `snap-declaration`. No repository or key decision.
82	
83	## Consequences
84	
85	**Positive**
86	- Provenance replicates, not just presence, and the guarantee is checked against the target's real state.
87	- Package managers stay authoritative for their own state.
88	- The review asks only what the user can answer.
89	
90	**Negative (costly to reverse)**
91	- Manifest schema, item identity and decision-file format are shaped by D-01; switching to file-level replication later replaces the whole job core.
92	- Package sync requires passwordless sudo on both machines.
93	- A repository or remote feeding no synced item does not travel: the two machines converge for what packages need, not to identical configurations.
94	- Pins always-sync, so a `preferences.d` file the user wanted on one machine returns every run unless deleted on the source.
95	- An unreproducible item is only as converged as its version string says.
96	
97	## Alternatives Considered
98	
99	- **File-level replication of the package databases** — rejected: managers must stay authoritative.
100	- **A single combined `package_sync` job** — rejected: independent enable flags, config, failure isolation.
101	- **A `--delete` file mirror of `/etc/apt`** — rejected: wipes the target's own machine-specific sources.
102	- **Repositories and remotes as reviewed items on top of an origin check** — rejected: keeps the unrepresentable "package ticked, repository unticked" pairing.
103	- **Deriving pins per package rather than always-syncing** — rejected: a pin naming an absent origin is inert, so precision buys nothing.
104	- **Always-syncing every flatpak remote** — rejected: a remote costs a summary fetch on every `flatpak update`.

## Summary

Fixes the illness surfaced in #271: package-sync docs were 3,800 lines / 108k words across five overlapping files, with the spec written twice. Scope grew in-review to also: strip GSD milestone phase numbers from code and docs, tighten ADR-021 to logging only, rewrite ADR-022 as subsystem-agnostic, and drop the colliding `D-nn` identifiers from ADRs and citations across the whole repo.

## Package-sync docs (the original ask)

| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `jobs/package-sync.md` | 485 lines, 71 avg w/para | 187 lines, 25 avg |
| `system/package-sync.md` | 183 lines of prose, 0 Lineage | 555 lines of ID'd articles with Lineage + Impl |
| `planning/package-sync-user-requirements.md` | 359 lines | 90 lines (PO-level intent only) |

| `adr-020` | 212 lines, 125 avg w/para | 128 lines, 36 avg |
| `adr-021` | 88 lines, 63 avg w/para | 91 lines, 20 avg (tightened + rewritten to logging-only) |
| `adr-022` | 137 lines, 62 avg w/para | 119 lines, 22 avg (rewritten subsystem-agnostic) |
| `adr-012` | — | amended with altitudes + rationale rule |
| `adr/considerations/package-sync-rationale.md` | — | new, 111 lines, keyed by article ID |
| `adr/considerations/adr-022-command-measurements.md` | — | new, 68 lines, per-command measurements ADR-022 used to inline |

## In-scope creep, each landed on this branch

**GSD phase numbers stripped.** `Phase 1`/`Phase 2`/… were milestone-scoped labels that rot the moment the next milestone starts numbering again. Removed 11 GSD-phase references from `src/`, `tests/` and `docs/`; the durable feature name (folder sync, package sync) is what replaces them. The internal validation-pipeline phases in `models.py`/`orchestrator.py` (schema → job config → system state) and the six workflow stages in `tests/self-update-test-playbook.md` are non-GSD uses and stay.

**ADR-021 rescoped to logging.** Was drifting into display-time redaction (prompts, review lines, file bodies) and reading as a closed enumeration of what pc-switcher logs. Now: adds content rules on top of ADR-010, does not define the whole set; separates the rule (no credential in the log) from the mechanism (URL-userinfo redaction at the log filter) from the accepted gap (package-sync snippet bodies are user-authored shell the tool does not parse).

**ADR-022 rewritten subsystem-agnostic.** Was package-sync-specific in everything but the title (`ProbeFailed`, `ConvergeItemFailed`, `packages/probes.py`, `AptProbe`). Now names only the general rule and mechanism. The concrete per-command measurements move to `adr/considerations/adr-022-command-measurements.md`.

**`D-nn` identifiers dropped.** `D-nn` collided across ADRs — `D-01` meant "convergence model" in ADR-020 and "the two categories" in ADR-022; `D-06` meant snap-revision in one and subsystem-failure-cap in the other. ADR-011 already prescribed semantic IDs for the golden record. ADR-020 and ADR-022 headings now use descriptive names only; all citations in `src/`, `tests/`, `docs/` use the semantic `PKG-FR-*` / `PKG-NG-*` article IDs from `docs/system/package-sync.md`.
